simple.meaning: עָקַשׁ (ʻâqash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to knot or distort ; figuratively, to pervert (act or declare perverse).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Job, Proverbs, Isaiah, Micah, beginning at Job 9:20. The surrounding contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָקַשׁ (H6140) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָקַשׁ (ʻâqash) / H6140 is traced through Job 9:20, Proverbs 10:9, Proverbs 28:18, Isaiah 59:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to knot or distort ; figuratively, to pervert (act or declare perverse)
definitions.full: H6140. aqash [ עָקַשׁ ] verb twist (Late Hebrew id. (rare)); — Niph`al Participle construct דְּרָכַיִם Prov 28:18 one crooked in ways (< plural, compare Toy). Pi`el Perfect 3plural לָהֶם עִקְּשׁז Isa 59:8 their paths they have twisted. Imperfect 3masculine plural יְעַקֵּ֑שׁזּ Micah 3:9 all that is straight they make crooked; Participle דְּרָכָיו מְעַקֵּשׁ Prov 10:9 (compare Niph`al ). Hiph`il Imperfect וַיּעְקְשֵׁנִי Job 9:20 (Ges § 53n ) he hath declared me crooked , devious (in life).
